name: BAXY
description: Voice and text assistant that operates a Windows PC in English and Spanish, running its own fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B model on a dedicated 4 GB GPU.
compatibility: Runs its model with llama-server from llama.cpp.
Speech recognition (Parakeet) and the voice (Supertonic 3) run on sherpa-onnx.
limitations: Needs a dedicated GPU with 4 GB of memory; integrated graphics and CPU only are not supported.
AMD support is partly tested: version 1.3.0 ran on one AMD card, but 1.3.1 was tested with a simulated AMD card. Intel cards were not tested.
Installing needs internet and about 12 GB free; the download is about 5 GB. The installer is unsigned, and downloading from the release page was not tested end to end for 1.3.1.
It acts on the desktop with the user's permissions. It asks before destructive actions, sending something or closing unsaved work, and that prompt can be turned off.
Web requests, and an optional third-party model API the user connects, send data off the PC; otherwise it stays local.
The project's own code is MIT. The voice model uses BigScience OpenRAIL-M, which restricts use; avatar media and other components have separate terms.

The maintainer reports unresolved licensing questions about the wake word model's training, including voices without written permission. Earlier releases were withdrawn; the 1.3.1 release notes describe the remaining uncertainty.
